title: The Deployment Challenge For Cheap Solar
gist: China now makes just shy of 90% of the world's solar modules but earns almost nothing doing it, with module margins near zero for 18 months on massive excess capacity. With panels commoditized, the economic value of solar shifts from manufacturing to installation, and the biggest local gains accrue to countries that can scale distributed generation at homes and businesses.

insights.claim: Chinese manufacturers now produce just shy of 90% of the world's solar modules and hold an even larger share of the upstream wafers and cells that go into them.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Any non-Chinese solar supply-chain or tariff strategy starts from near-total dependence; upstream wafer/cell concentration is the tighter chokepoint than modules themselves.
insights.quote: Its manufacturers now produce just shy of 90% of the world’s solar modules, and are even more dominant in the wafers and cells that make up those modules.
insights.locator: For most of the past two decades

insights.claim: Massive excess capacity has pushed solar module profit margins to near zero, where they have bounced around for the past 18 months.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Market-share dominance is not translating into profit — treat Chinese module makers as volume proxies with no earnings power until capacity actually exits.
insights.quote: module profit margins have been bouncing around near zero for the past 18 months

insights.claim: Winning the solar manufacturing race has not produced a profitable industry, implying that owning panel production is a poor way to capture the economics of the energy transition.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Cautions against equating industrial-policy dominance with investable returns; favor exposure downstream rather than in cell/module capacity.

themes.theme: Value migrates from panel to installation

insights.claim: The two-decade era in which the solar story was about making the panel cheaper is over, because China has already solved the cost problem.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Reframes solar research and capital allocation away from module cost curves toward deployment bottlenecks — permitting, grid connection, labor, financing.
insights.quote: For most of the past two decades, the solar story was about making the panel cheaper. China has solved that problem.
insights.locator: For most of the past two decades

insights.claim: With solar equipment now a commodity, the economic value of solar will mainly come from its installation rather than from making the hardware.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Points investors toward installers, EPC, balance-of-system and deployment-services businesses as the margin pool, with panels as a deflating input cost.
insights.quote: With equipment now a commodity, the economic value of solar will mainly come from its installation.

themes.theme: Distributed generation as the deployment edge

insights.claim: The broadest local economic benefits from cheap solar are likely to accrue to countries that figure out how to scale up distributed generation at homes and businesses.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Country-level solar winners should be screened on rooftop/distributed deployment capability, not on installed utility-scale capacity or domestic manufacturing.
insights.quote: The broadest local benefits are likely to come in countries that can figure out how to scale up distributed solar generation at homes and businesses.
insights.locator: The broadest local benefits are likely

insights.claim: The binding constraint on solar is now deployment capacity — the ability of a country to physically install cheap panels — rather than the supply or price of the panels themselves.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Watch installation-rate data and distributed-solar policy as the leading indicator of which markets convert cheap modules into real energy-cost advantage.
insights.locator: The Deployment Challenge For Cheap Solar
